## What it is

Umami counts visits to your websites (pages, referrers, countries, devices) without cookies and without collecting personal data, as a self-hosted alternative to Google Analytics ([umami-software/umami](https://github.com/umami-software/umami)).

**Licence:** `MIT` (GitHub licence API). Market class **L1**. There is no license-matrix row yet, so the gate notes that it is not preinstallable on sold boxes until one is added (brief 30 B10).

**Icon:** a neutral generated icon with initials; no upstream logo is shipped.

## Market listing

- Category and sub-tags (docs/design/TAXONOMY.md §1): monitoring: analytics. The sub-tags go into `metadata.tags` once the schema has it.
- Deployment class (TAXONOMY §2): **Market · community** until CI writes a passing scan (contract §9.4), then Market · verified if every check passes.

## How it runs here

- One `Deployment` (`Recreate`) with Umami and PostgreSQL 15 (the version upstream's compose file uses) as a native sidecar on 127.0.0.1 only. PostgreSQL trusts local connections, so there is no database password and no Secret.
- `APP_SECRET` (required; Umami refuses to start without it) and `TWO_FACTOR_ENCRYPTION_KEY` (256-bit, for two-factor sign-in) are generated once by an init container onto the database volume and loaded by the container command before upstream's start script.
- Non-root: Umami as the image's `nextjs` user (UID 1001), PostgreSQL as UID 999. No privilege escalation, all capabilities dropped.
- Volume: `umami-db` (10 GiB).
- Probes: `GET /api/heartbeat` (upstream's compose health check).

## First run

Source: [Umami README](https://github.com/umami-software/umami/blob/v3.5.0/README.md) and [umami.is/docs](https://umami.is/docs).

1. Install Umami from the Market and approve the action. It installs into `app-umami`.
2. Forward the port and open http://localhost:3000:
   ```sh
   kubectl -n app-umami port-forward svc/umami 3000:3000
   ```
3. Sign in with the account the first start creates, "username **admin** and password **umami**", and change the password when asked.
4. Add a website and copy its tracking snippet into your site.

## Not done yet

- **Tracking needs a reachable address:** visitors' browsers load the tracking script from Umami and send events to it, so a public website needs Umami exposed publicly, which is a separate, owner-approved step (TAXONOMY §3.1 exposure) that does not exist yet. Until then it can count visits to sites on your home network only once the app proxy gives it a LAN address.
- No HTTPS or LAN hostname: OneMind v0 has no ingress or certificates for apps, so the dashboard is reached through a port-forward until the app proxy exists.
- `readOnlyRootFilesystem` is not set: the start script updates the tracker file in the image.
- Resource figures are OneMind choices; upstream publishes none. They are checked against real use when the CI smoke test (contract §9.4 check 9) runs.
- `metadata.tier` stays `community` until `sdk/tools/app-gate` in CI writes a passing `scan.json`. `spec.updates.automerge` is `none` until `renovate.json` lists the app.

## Why this app is blocked

The CI app gate (`sdk/tools/app-gate`, contract §9.4) computed tier **blocked** for this app on 2026-11-12 (ci-apps run 43212771377, job `gate (umami)`). The gateway lists a blocked app in the Market but refuses to install it (§10.3, §11.1). The app is kept, not hidden, and the gate was not weakened. Reasons from that run:

- Vulnerability: `docker.io/library/postgres:15.19-trixie`: CVE-2025-68121 in the Go `stdlib` v1.24.6, fixed in 1.24.13, 1.25.7 or 1.26.0-rc.3.
- Secret finding (Trivy): the same postgres image has `private-key` (HIGH) in `/etc/ssl/private/ssl-cert-snakeoil.key` (Debian's ssl-cert package).
- Licence: GitHub MIT matches, but there is no research licence-matrix row, so the app is not preinstallable on sold boxes until one is added (brief 30 B10).
- Passed: ClamAV (0 infected), smoke test (GET / returned 200).

To unblock: move the pins to upstream releases that fix these findings (tags that exist, checked with `crane`), then rerun `sdk/tools/app-gate` (the daily `apps-rescan` workflow does this too). Nothing is bumped to an unverified tag.
